Preserve the prior review as evidence and independently check it. Actual canonical Baton source: /run/baton2-native-homelab/retained/baton2-compiler-741-20261015/postrelease-751-761-20261015-9/source, production commit b1f006a6308bbb00e29a24322e4f7d5164774470. Current installed Baton 2.0 is the coordination tool; source under review includes newer changes. The pinned compiler source/runtime is in that build root's toolchain-home/bend2. Separate shipped behavior, source-only work, proposed extensions and paper-reported results. A separate root lane owns current release qualification and actual Bend2 REPL implementation (#778); no full coordinator builds or release edits here.
All work executes on this authorized homelab runner. Preserve existing jobs, credentials, native profiles, source revisions, full failures and raw evidence. Read-only source review and primary research are authorized. Small isolated remote probes can be written under /run/baton2-native-homelab/retained/baton-cli-orchestra-20261016/deliverables/YOUR_SESSION, retaining all source, complete outputs, commands, revisions and actual exit results. Do not edit the shared source checkouts, build the full coordinator, change credentials/profiles, signal processes, mutate live project knowledge stores, or create branches. Proposed doc revisions belong in your own deliverables directory or complete inline Baton reports; root will review and integrate them. Task text belongs in Baton; do not create Markdown task input files.
Operator requirements: actual Bend2 implementation/language; concise action-verb agent commands; Baton owns inferable control identity and automatic message handling; all sessions receive the existing randomized initialization seed; no ambient step/token/time quotas or arbitrary ceilings; preserve authority, lineage, alternatives and complete evidence; commit/push/merge completed validated work through the authorized root. Runtime limitations must be proven against actual source and smallest experiments. Treat changes to these requirements as explicit design conflicts, not implicit recommendations. Research citations must identify primary sources, actual full-text evidence and limitations. Write plain technical English. Use your native harness todo tool to track your full assignment and update it as you work.
Use contextual Baton inbox, dispatch, report, send, finish and confirm commands discovered through help. Baton-generated identities stay under program control; no manual acknowledgement commands. Registered DB is /run/baton2-native-homelab/retained/baton-cli-orchestra-20261016/orchestra.db; current session context supplies your actor. Complete reports must include source revision/path evidence, severity, reproducible failure or evidence, alternative hypotheses, the strongest case for the proposal, concrete corrections, costs, experiments and unresolved dissent. Read peer work only after recording your independent findings, then critique and revise. Native turn completion when waiting lets Baton deliver later peer input; remain assigned until your coordinator confirms completion.

You are Associate Conductor evidence-lead, own tight Ensemble evidence-research, and report to proposal-root. Your two existing registered workers are listed below, with their native receivers ready. Dispatch their complete task guidance through Baton now, including this shared scope and their specialty. Collect their independent reports, cross-assign critiques, perform your own source review and strengthen/reject conclusions using evidence. Preserve disagreements. Coordinate with evidence-lead, runtime-lead and design-lead through tight proposal-deliberation; exchange substantive reports, not status-only notices. Additional subordinate contributors/Ensembles are authorized when they resolve an actual uncovered question, using existing authorized routes, resources and preserved evidence.
Worker citation-auditor (omp, zai/glm-5.3-flash): Audit the entire local research corpus and design claims against primary papers and pinned implementation sources. Recheck all numerical comparisons, omitted baselines, citations, evidence grades, and claims in the existing seven-agent audit. Deliver a complete claim register with source URLs/locations, revisions, uncertainty, corrections and consequences.

Worker research-critic (omp, zai/glm-5.3-flash): Research primary literature and implementations relevant to asynchronous agents, long-horizon reliability, context architectures, programmatic tools, self-extension, capability security, evaluation and the randomized initialization seed. Find strong counterexamples, failed replications, boundary conditions and competing explanations. Read actual papers and official source; abstracts alone cannot support detailed claims. Design discriminating experiments and state costs and evidence limits.
After the first independent round, send your complete synthesis and the underlying reports to the other two Conductors and proposal-root. Deliberate over conflicting conclusions. Produce revised proposed design text, a claim register, concrete experiments, source-linked follow-up issues/todos, accepted corrections, unresolved alternatives, and a clear map of changes to current Baton/Bend2. Do not force consensus or copy prior audit verdicts without rechecking. Your own completion requires reviewed subordinate results and peer deliberation. Root confirms completion after reviewing the full result.

All confirmed boundaries enter the register as R6 scope caveats.

It upgrades the token half from unmeasured to unmeasured-with-one-measured-adverse-prior (2.1:1) but does not defeat the narrowing: those costs are harness-driven speculation machinery absent from model-driven async transcript design, the paper scopes the trade as regime-dependent, and bet 1 falsification concerns turn structure which none of the three papers measures. The revised section 5 previously implied that a generated program's nested calls re-entering over loopback mean 'the child holds no authority the seat did not grant'. Provider-side, a seed does not make agent runs reproducible (OpenAI documents best-effort sampling determinism; Anthropic documents infrastructure noise worth up to 6 points on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and recommends skepticism below 3-point leaderboard gaps, prescribing resource-band calibration and temporal averaging, not seeding; none of Harbor, Terminal-Bench 4.0, or the Anthropic page uses or endorses rollout seeds). Miller (arXiv:2411.00640) shows temperature reduction does not fix eval variance while resampling, paired differences, and power analysis do. The sketch bet-settling protocol specifies same model and pinned harness but no trial counts, no error bars, no seed policy; Harbor-Index at 82 tasks and 3 trials has a paired minimum detectable effect near 11 points (probe in deliverables/research-critic/probes/seed-variance), so amendment 16 needs a power statement and amendment 19 should add recorded per-arm trial counts and paired-difference standard errors. Session seed and evaluation seed are distinct instruments.
